literal: The king who has the painful reputation spoken of him saying 'the ruler is cruel', his lifetime having shortened, will quickly perish.
translation: A king who earns the painful reputation of being called a cruel ruler will find his lifetime shortened and will quickly perish.
modern: நம் அரசன் கொடியவன் என்று மக்களால் பேசப்படும் துன்பகரமான சொல்லைப் பெற்ற அரசன், தன் ஆயுள் காலம் குறைந்து விரைந்து அழிவான்.
explanation: This couplet warns rulers against the dangers of being perceived as tyrannical. When subjects speak of their king as harsh or cruel ('இறைகடியன்'), this painful reputation ('இன்னாச்சொல்') acts as a destructive force. The word 'உறை' in this context refers to the king's span of life or reign. The couplet explains that such a ruler's lifetime is hastened ('கடுகி') to an end, leading to his swift ('ஒல்லை') ruin.
